hints.title: Endpoint Independence
hints.text: Substrings starting and ending with the same character are formed by choosing any two identical character positions or a single character.

hints.title: Combinatorial Counting
hints.text: If a letter appears C times across the string, calculate the number of valid pairs using the formula C * (C + 1) // 2.

hints.title: Single Pass Summation
hints.text: Accumulate counts per character and sum the triangular numbers for each character frequency.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: For each character with total count C, C * (C + 1) // 2 matching substrings exist.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all substrings in O(N^2) time is redundant because pairs of matching endpoints can be counted directly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant extra memory for twenty-six character counts avoids nested iterations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should express the combination count as C * (C + 1) // 2 per unique character.
